newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania leu treads lower in squeezed market.
newsitem.headline: Romania leu treads lower in squeezed market.

text.p: The Romanian leu currency inched down on Thursday to 5,650/720 against the dollar from 5,550/700 in early trading on an interbank market struggling to cope with increasing hard currency shortages.
"Hard currency offer gets lower and lower. Everybody is queueing for some bucks, but sellers continue to keep to the sidelines," said a trader.
Operators said the leu might gain some support at the weekend from Thursday's rise in the central bank's one-week rate to 70 percent from 65 as part of a recent drive to tighten monetary policy.
"The leu is poised to head towards 6,000 by the end of the month as the country's export earnings remain low," said a trader with one of the four market-making dealer banks.
Leu-dollar retail rates ranged from 6,000/100 to 6,275/500, and traders said the dollar demand was on the rise amid inflationary expectations.
Traders said the money market was bracing for higher prices in response to the surge in the central bank's one-week rate.
